context: Morgan invests a sum of money (in rand) into an account which pays compound interest, compounded annually, and pays out a lump sum at the end of a whole number of years. Given the amount invested, the number of years and the lump sum he receives, find the annual compound interest rate the bank offered. The rate is a whole-number percentage, so the n-th root comes out exactly.

params.why: the lump sum must be an exact number of cents, so the rate is exactly r % and the root is exact

stem: Morgan invests $\text{R{=P}}$ into an account which pays out a lump sum at the end of ${=n}$ years. If he gets $\text{R{=fixed(A, 2)}}$ at the end of the period, what compound interest rate did the bank offer him? The interest is compounded annually. Give the rate as a percentage per annum, as a number without the % sign.
solution: Write down what is given: $A=\text{R{=fixed(A, 2)}}$, $P=\text{R{=P}}$, $n={=n}$ and $i=\,?$
Write down the formula and substitute the known values: $A=P(1+i)^{n}$ gives $\text{R{=fixed(A, 2)}}=\text{R{=P}}(1+i)^{{=n}}$
Divide both sides by $\text{R{=P}}$ to get the bracket on its own: $\frac{{=fixed(A, 2)}}{{=P}}=(1+i)^{{=n}}$
Take the $n$th root of both sides (here $n={=n}$) and use your calculator: $1+i=\sqrt[{=n}]{\frac{{=fixed(A, 2)}}{{=P}}}={=fixed(g, 2)}$
Subtract $1$ from both sides to find $i$: $i={=fixed(g, 2)}-1={=fixed(r / 100, 2)}$
Write the rate as a percentage: $i\times 100={=r}$, so the bank offered a compound interest rate of ${=r}$ % p.a.
Check: $\text{R{=P}}\times({=fixed(g, 2)})^{{=n}}=\text{R{=fixed(A, 2)}}$, which is the amount Morgan received.
notes: Basic tier: the entry point of 'solve A = P(1+i)^n for i', modelled on ex9-2-7 (Morgan, R5000 to R7500) but with data chosen so that the rate is an exact whole percentage and the n-th root is clean. n is 3 or 4 so the root is written with the book's \sqrt[n] notation (n = 2 would print the unconventional \sqrt[2]); for n = 4 only 10 % and 20 % keep the lump sum exact to the cent. The require guarantees A = P(1+r/100)^n is an exact amount of rand and cents (checked offline: 72 distinct (n, r, P) combinations, A at most R41472.00, and the n-th root of A/P equals 1 + r/100 exactly in every one), so there is exactly one correct answer and no rounding is involved. The stem says the interest is compounded annually, to match the formula A = P(1+i)^n, and asks for the percentage as a bare number, as the book's answers are (e.g. 8.45). No mcq, so no distractors; the catalogued misconception (reading a very high rate as a mistake in the working) belongs to the advanced we06 comment question, which is a book question and is not repeated here. Standard and advanced tiers are not gaps (four book questions already cover them), and a non-exact root cannot be computed with the available expression language, so no rounded-decimal family is offered.
